summary: Restoration pledges are mainly EU-level: by 2030, measures should cover at least 20% of EU land and 20% of EU sea areas, and by 2050 they should cover all ecosystems needing restoration. Rewetting peatlands and wetlands is estimated to provide 51-54 Mt CO2-eq/yr, while reforestation and sustainable forest management, which combine restoration and conservation, are estimated at 8-235 Mt CO2-eq/yr. Conservation sets an EU LULUCF net-removals target of 310 Mt CO2-eq by 2030 (shown as -310 Mt in carbon-sinks accounting), 42 Mt above the 2016-2018 average. Agriculture includes a 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr EU mitigation potential from improved fertiliser efficiency. The Netherlands' LULUCF allocation is -435 Kt CO2eq by 2030. For scale, 20% of its 35,046 km2 land area is about 7,009 km2; forest, grassland, agriculture and wetlands cover 10.0%, 37.8%, 35.3% and 1.4%, respectively, but the quoted percentage and mitigation potentials are EU-wide, not Dutch area targets.
